analysis:
The supplied changes to docs/provider/cli-reference.md are documentation only: a date bump (line 3), a new paragraph on drain behavior with the coordinator connection down and a 15 s per-model unload bound (head ~926-932), and a revised `doctor` bullet about configuration changes needing a restart (head ~998-1013). No executable code, key handling, attestation, authorization or encryption logic changes in this file. The base unit (lines 1726-1974) and the head unit (lines 1-397) are excerpts. The changed head ranges around 926-1013 are not visible in the head text, so the exact wording of the new drain paragraph and the doctor bullet was not seen in full beyond the patch excerpt, which is truncated.

Security-relevant reading of the visible patch: the documented behavior lets a drain with no unfinished work finish without a coordinator acknowledgement when the connection is down, justified because the disconnect already cancelled accepted work. This touches TB-002 and T-010 (cancellation and drain) and T-053 (stale authorization surviving a connection change). It is documentation of existing provider behavior (`ProviderLoop.unloadAllModelsForShutdown`), and the supplied evidence does not show a code change or an inconsistency with the threat model. The statement that a model whose native retirement never finishes is left to process exit is an availability and residual-data note related to T-028 (residual GPU memory). It is consistent with process-exit cleanup and is not a regression.

The visible base text (cache paths, prefix-cache env gates, LaunchAgent passthrough) is unchanged in this PR. It is consistent with T-041: default-on SSD cache, 30-minute TTL, kill switch DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0. Remaining integration questions: whether the code actually implements the documented 10 s wait and the acknowledgement-skip path without dropping a queued coordinator usage or settlement message. The provider source is not supplied, so that cannot be verified here. No findings are reported.
